segments.text: Why a bomb calorimeter measures ΔU · measured: q_V = −C ΔT
segments.spoken: A bomb calorimeter measures q V, the heat of a reaction at constant volume, from a temperature rise. Why is that delta U?

segments.text: rigid steel walls: they cannot move · ΔV = 0
segments.spoken: The bomb's steel walls are rigid. They cannot move, so the volume stays constant: delta V is zero.

segments.text: the gases cannot push the walls outward · w = 0
segments.spoken: When the sample burns, the gases cannot push the walls outward, so no expansion work is done: w is zero.

segments.text: first law: ΔU = q + w · w = 0, so ΔU = q_V
segments.spoken: The first law says delta U equals q plus w. With w zero, delta U equals q V.

segments.text: A bomb calorimeter measures the change in internal energy: ΔU = q_V = −C ΔT
segments.spoken: So a bomb calorimeter measures the change in internal energy: delta U equals q V equals minus C delta T.
